items.teaser: The death toll from a Russian airstrike on October 29 in Izium, Kharkiv region, has risen to five; a Day of Mourning has been declared in the community.

items.title: Power supply situation is difficult in Kyiv and Dnipropetrovsk and Kyiv oblasts, says Energy Ministry
items.teaser: Repair crews have resumed the electricity supply to critical infrastructure and some consumers in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, while repairs continue in Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast. Extensive damage and the threat of further attacks are delaying the work.

items.title: Evacuees from Oleshky head to Russia before flying to Belarus – video
items.teaser: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky are heading home via Anapa and Belarus with Ukrainian officials as part of an agreed humanitarian corridor.

items.title: Putin open to phone call with Zelensky, Ukraine suspects a Kremlin trap
items.teaser: The Kremlin is seeking to avoid a face-to-face meeting between President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin by proposing they speak by phone instead, the Kyiv Independent has learned. items.title: Russia has damaged more than 800 Ukrainian energy assets since September
items.teaser: Russia has carried out more than 350 attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure since September, damaging more than 800 pieces of equipment, Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said on Friday.

items.title: Ukraine’s SOF ambush enemy in Russia and seize documents
items.teaser: Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces (SOF) carried out an ambush on the territory of the Russian Federation, destroying a vehicle and seizing enemy documents.

items.title: Spezialeinsatzkräfte legen in Russland Hinterhalt und erbeuten Dokumente des Feindes
items.teaser: Spezialeinsatzkräfte legten einen Hinterhalt auf russischem Territorium, zerstörten ein Fahrzeug und erbeuteten Dokumente des Feindes.

items.title: Manufacturer of Ruta cruise missiles used by Ukraine's defence forces reveals production figures – video
items.teaser: European company Destinus says it has produced 1,750 Ruta B1 cruise missiles, with monthly output nearing 300 units and a range of over 300 km.

items.title: One injured, apartment buildings and school damaged in Russian strike on Dnipro
items.teaser: A woman was injured in Dnipro as a result of a Russian attack this afternoon.

items.title: NATO top commander sees no delays in delivery of Patriot missiles to Ukraine
items.teaser: NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe General Alexus Grynkewich said the United States continues to supply Ukraine with Patriot interceptor missiles, as well as weapons packages paid for by European allies.

items.title: Dozens of Russian drones fell to gun turrets over Kyiv in a month, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry says
items.teaser: The ministry also credits turrets with 60+ targets in a private project—the figure it gave on 14 October for all private teams.

items.teaser: Polish authorities investigate whether a Russian national detained in Świdnica transferred quarter of a million photos of vital transport networks to foreign intelligence.

items.title: Russia strikes Kharkiv shopping centre with jet-powered drone, forcing temporary closure
items.teaser: A Russian Shahed-type UAV has hit the roof of the Dafi shopping centre in Kharkiv, forcing the facility to temporarily suspend its operations.

items.title: Another Russian “state-of-the-art” Su-57 fighter burned at Akhtubinsk, apparently without anyone shooting at it
items.teaser: A malfunction at engine start is the reported cause, leaving a burn scar visible from orbit and one fewer stealth jet in Russia’s small fleet.

items.title: Russian drone strikes enterprise in Shostka, killing one and injuring eight
items.teaser: A 43-year-old woman was killed and eight people were injured, one of them seriously, in a Russian drone strike on a civilian enterprise in the town of Shostka, Sumy region.

items.title: Russia’s Geran-5 has hit 1,000 km/h in maneuvers, and Chinese engineers help develop some technical solutions for Russia’s drones
items.teaser: Ukrainian firms have shown jet interceptors but hit trouble with guidance, target lock, and scaling up, the adviser said.

items.title: Angriff auf Dnipro: Fünf Hochhäuser und eine Schule beschädigt, eine Person verletzt
items.teaser: Bei einem Angriff russischer Besatzungstruppen am Nachmittag wurde in der Stadt Dnipro eine Frau verletzt.

items.title: Poland detains man suspected of stabbing two Ukrainians in ethnically-motivated attack
items.teaser: Polish police have announced the arrest of a 30-year-old man suspected of stabbing two passengers on a city bus in Warsaw.

items.title: Poland may reconsider transferring additional MiG-29s to Ukraine if Bulgaria deal falls through – expert
items.teaser: Poland is transferring two MiG-29 fighter jets to Ukraine, while talks with Bulgaria on transferring the remaining aircraft of this type are still ongoing. If an agreement with Sofia cannot be reached, Warsaw may reconsider transferring the jets to Ukraine.

items.title: Russia set to return to international hockey tournaments after top sports court's ruling
items.teaser: The sports court's ruling means that Russia will be able to participate in a sweep of forthcoming ice hockey tournaments in Canada, Czechia, the U.S., and Germany.

items.title: 'They killed us' – Pressure from Russian authorities forces closure of Novaya Gazeta
items.teaser: "This is not just our personal story. This is the story of a country and a society that are being crushed in exactly the same way," the Novaya Gazeta staff wrote.

items.title: Spionagefall Hanning - Medien: US-Dienste prüfen Zusammenarbeit mit BND
items.teaser: Der mutmaßliche Spionagefall um den früheren Präsidenten des Bundesnachrichtendienstes, Hanning, sorgt offenbar für Unruhe bei internationalen Partnerdiensten.

items.title: The Pentagon wants NATO’s eastern flank to be quiet about Russia while Washington courts Moscow
items.teaser: Ukraine has already felt the same pressure, aimed at its strikes rather than its words.

items.title: Russian strike on Sumy Oblast kills 1, injures 8 people

items.teaser: As a result of Russian attacks since September, more than 800 pieces of power generation equipment have been damaged.

items.teaser: The Dutch-headquartered company also says it expects to be able to meet Europe’s demand, including Ukraine’s, for 1.5-kilonewton-class cruise-missile engines from next year.

items.title: Ukraine zerstört Iskander- Abschussrampe in der russischen Region Kursk

items.teaser: The Russians in occupied Crimea are training children and young people to fly drones, fire assault rifles and take them apart. Ukrainian intelligence says the training uses drones and other equipment belonging to the Russian military.

items.title: Shadows, roofs, job ads give Ukrainian arms plants away to Russian analysts, Ukrainian experts warn
items.teaser: In 2022, a pro-Russian Telegram channel posted the location of a Kyiv tank workshop. Russian missiles hit it two days later.

items.title: They rescued passengers during evacuation: five railway employees killed in strike on Dnipro train station
items.teaser: Ukrzaliznytsia has revealed the stories of five of its employees who lost their lives when a Russian drone hit a train platform in Dnipro on 29 October.

items.title: Russian drone strikes building in center of Novhorod-Siverskyi
items.teaser: Russian troops struck a building in the central part of the city of Novhorod-Siverskyi in the Chernihiv region with a drone during the day.

items.title: Defense forces strike Iskander-M launcher in Russia’s Kursk region
items.teaser: On October 29 and during the night of October 30, the Ukrainian Defense Forces struck an “Iskander-M” tactical missile system launcher in the Kursk Oblast of the Russian Federation, as well as ammunition depots, logistics facilities, and repair units of the Russian Army.

items.title: UP: Kravchenko stopped at border over NABU and SAPO flag, let through after call from Kyiv
items.teaser: According to Ukrainska Pravda sources, then-prosecutor general Ruslan Kravchenko was prevented from crossing into Poland at the Shehyni crossing point due to a flag from the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO), but was allowed through followin

items.title: Hilfstransporte für die ukrainische Frontstadt Oleschky laufen an
items.teaser: Die Bewohner der von Russland besetzten ukrainischen Frontstadt Oleschky können jetzt mit Hilfe rechnen. Die Route ist von Minen geräumt, die Versorgung mit Hilfslieferungen hat begonnen. Die Waffenruhe gilt noch bis Sonntag.

items.title: NATO says it has much to learn from Ukraine in field of innovation
items.teaser: The NATO Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic and Ukraine have inked an agreement to jointly develop and test military technologies.

items.title: Ukrainian officials reach Russian-held Oleshky. The question now is where its residents can go
items.teaser: Agreement pages send residents who choose Ukraine through Russia and Belarus, and Ukraine's ombudsman is set to travel the same route.

items.title: Polens Polizei fasst mutmaßlichen russischen Agenten
items.teaser: Ein Russe fotografiert in Schlesien Züge und Bahnanlagen – auf seinen Speichern finden Ermittler Hunderttausende Dateien.

items.title: Head of the President's Office: Humanitarian operation underway in Oleshky, transport arranged
items.teaser: The head of the Ukrainian President's Office has confirmed that relief supplies have reached occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast and vehicles are prepared for civilian evacuation.

items.title: Russian drones kill woman in Sumy Oblast
items.teaser: Russian strike drones attacked Shostka in Sumy Oblast, killing a 43-year-old woman and injuring eight people, one in a serious condition, the mayor says.

items.title: Russian ballistic missiles kill a man in Kyiv, capping a day that left at least 27 civilians dead across Ukraine
items.teaser: The night also blacked out Dnipro, where people were still mourning the victims of the day before.

items.title: Humanitarian aid reaches residents of Oleshky
items.teaser: Humanitarian aid has been delivered to residents of the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky in the Kherson region.

items.title: Verteidigungsministerium: über 1000 russische Schnellboote und Schiffe seit Jahresbeginn getroffen
items.teaser: Seit Beginn des Jahres haben die Einheiten der ukrainischen Verteidigungskräfte 1.039 Schnellboote und Schiffe der russischen Armee mithilfe unbemannter Luftfahrzeuge zerstört oder außer Gefecht gesetzt, teilte das Verteidigungsministerium mit.

items.title: Rozetka marketplace store damaged in Russian attack on Kyiv
items.teaser: A Rozetka marketplace store in Kyiv's Dniprovskyi district has been damaged in a Russian missile strike.

items.title: UP finds that Odesa businessman may have sheltered fugitive prosecutor general Kravchenko in Vienna
items.teaser: Ukrainska Pravda's investigation suggests Volodymyr Halanternyk helped former prosecutor general Kravchenko settle in Vienna and that his staff gave police statements against UP journalists.

items.title: It was the only transport serving a village where more than 1,600 people still live: Russian forces strike a social bus with a drone in Bilenke, killing a woman and injuring other passengers
items.teaser: At the time of the attack, the bus was carrying a driver and 23 passengers, most of them elderly, the head of the humanitarian organization said.

items.title: Russia: Critical newspaper 'Novaya Gazeta' to close
items.teaser: "Novaya Gazeta," one of the last remaining independent, critical media outlets in Russia, has announced it is closing under pressure from state authorities. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, evacuations have begun in Oleshky.

items.title: Russian forces strike facility in Chernihiv
items.teaser: On Friday, October 30, Russian troops attacked a facility in Chernihiv, causing a vehicle on the premises to catch fire.

items.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
items.teaser: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: 1590 Soldaten: Russlands Verluste seit gestern
items.teaser: Die Zahl der getöteten oder verletzten russischen Soldaten ist seit dem 24. Februar 2022 auf 1. 586. 500 gestiegen. Allein innerhalb von 24 Stunden beträgt die Zahl der Verluste 1590.

items.title: Russian forces strike Dnipro again
items.teaser: The enemy army struck Dnipro.

items.title: Meeting is what matters: Zelenskyy's office responds to idea of phone call with Kremlin
items.teaser: Ukrainian presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn said Moscow's talk of phone calls or visits to Moscow is meant to avoid a trilateral leaders' meeting, which Ukraine wants.

items.title: Kyiv begins work on additional crossings over Dnipro River
items.teaser: Work has begun in Kyiv to provide additional bridge crossings over the Dnipro River, with the first expected to be ready early next year.

items.title: Ukrainische Delegation in Oleschky eingetroffen: Evakuierung beginnt – Arachamia
items.teaser: Die ukrainische Delegation ist in der besetzten Stadt Oleschky in der Region Cherson eingetroffen. Die Evakuierung und die Verteilung von humanitärer Hilfe haben begonnen, teilt der Vorsitzende der Parlamentsfraktion "Diener des Volkes", David Arachamia, auf Telegram mit.

items.title: Trump greets children dressed in Russian costumes at White House Halloween event
items.teaser: Two children dressed in Soviet military uniform and traditional Russian costume were among those greeted by Donald and Melania Trump at the White House Halloween event.

items.title: Eralp nach "Spiegel"-Bericht: "Werde mich von niemandem einschüchtern lassen"
items.teaser: Die Berliner Linken-Politikerin Elif Eralp hat am Donnerstag in einem Statement bekräftigt, in einer Regierung klar gegen Organisierte Kriminalität und Terror vorgehen zu wollen. Der "Spiegel" hatte zuvor berichtet, Eralp habe Angst vor Terror-Sympathisanten.

items.title: Russian forces strike business in Chernihiv
items.teaser: A fire broke out at a business in Chernihiv following a Russian attack.

items.title: Ukraine imposes new sanctions on Russia's Rassvet satellite system, 39 shadow fleet vessels
items.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has enacted a National Security and Defense Council decision imposing sanctions on Russian companies and individuals involved in developing the Rassvet satellite communications system, as well as on 39 vessels belonging to Russia's shadow fleet.

items.title: Russen greifen Einkaufszentrum in Charkiw an: vier Menschen verletzt
items.teaser: Das russische Militär hat ein Einkaufszentrum In Charkiw gezielt angegriffen. Vier Frauen wurden verletz,t teilt der Leiter der regionalen Militärverwaltung, Oleg Synehubow, auf Telegram mit.

items.title: „Interne Nachricht von Eralp ist erschütternd“: Leserdebatte zu Berliner Regierungsfrage
items.teaser: Leser diskutieren über Elif Eralps Sicherheitsbedenken, ihre Positionen zu Polizei und Verfassungsschutz sowie mögliche Koalitionen.

items.title: Ukrainian military strikes over 1,000 Russian boats and speedboats with drones since early 2026

items.teaser: "Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to leave safely. At the same time, those who have decided to stay can stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian support," Ukraine's Human Rights Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said.

items.teaser: As of the morning of October 30, consumers in Kyiv and four regions were left without electricity due to Russian attacks. Power consumption restrictions of up to 2.5 scheduled outage slots are in effect in parts of Ukraine.

items.title: Russia's legal siege over assets continues, costing Euroclear hundreds of millions of euros in 2026
items.teaser: Euroclear is facing "multiple proceedings in Russian courts," including a case launched by the Russian Central Bank that seeks to challenge the immobilization of its assets.

items.teaser: In den vergangenen 24 Stunden haben entlang der Front 211 Zusammenstöße zwischen den ukrainischen und russischen Streitkräften stattgefunden, die meisten – bei Kostjantyniwka, Pokrowsk und Hulajpole, teilt der ukrainische Generalstab auf Facebook mit.

items.title: Ukrainian PM: Number of people leaving Oleshky will be announced later
